title: Korat Marathon 2026 Review: Racing in Thailand's Isaan Gateway City
seo_title: Korat Marathon 2026 Review | Nakhon Ratchasima, Thailand
meta_description: Korat Marathon 2026 review: November 8 in Nakhon Ratchasima -- the third-largest city in Thailand and gateway to the Isaan region.
dek: Set for 8 November 2026, this marathon runs through Nakhon Ratchasima -- commonly called Korat -- Thailand's third-largest city and the historic gateway between Siam and Laos.
verdict: The Korat Marathon runs through Nakhon Ratchasima, Thailand's third-largest city and the largest in the entire Northeastern (Isaan) region, with a population of over 466,000. That's genuinely substantial city infrastructure to support a large-field race, positioned at the western edge of the Korat Plateau and serving as the transportation, commercial and governmental centre for northeastern Thailand. Four distances from 5K to the full marathon give it broad accessibility, and it's listed with AIMS World Running -- a mark of international race-calendar recognition.

sections.heading: Thailand's Third-Largest City
paragraphs: The Korat Marathon offers four distances: 5K, 10K, 21.1K and the 42.195K full marathon in Nakhon Ratchasima. [1] Nakhon Ratchasima, commonly known as Korat, is the capital of its province and the third-largest city in all of Thailand, with a population of 466,098 as of 2021. [2] That scale gives the race genuinely substantial infrastructure -- hotels, transport, road networks -- well beyond what most smaller-town races in this research batch can offer.

sections.heading: The Gateway to Isaan
paragraphs: Korat sits 250km northeast of Bangkok at the western edge of the Korat Plateau, historically marking the boundary between Lao and Siamese territory and serving today as the gateway to Thailand's Lao-speaking northeast (Isaan) region. [2] As the largest city in Northeastern Thailand and the region's transportation, commercial, financial and governmental centre, it's a genuinely significant urban hub rather than a secondary provincial stop.

sections.heading: International Race-Calendar Recognition
paragraphs: The race is listed with AIMS World Running (the Association of International Marathons and Distance Races), alongside its own official site. [1] That kind of international calendar listing -- shared with the Maybank Marathon in Bali covered elsewhere in this research -- is a meaningful signal of organisational standards and certification.

sections.heading: Registration Open, No Independent Reviews Yet
paragraphs: Registration is currently open. No independent participant reviews were found in research for this specific event, though the city's scale and AIMS listing suggest a reasonably mature operation rather than a speculative first-year event.

sections.heading: Should You Run It?
paragraphs: If you want a marathon in a genuinely major regional Thai city with real infrastructure and international race-calendar recognition, the Korat Marathon on 8 November 2026 is a solid, credible pick. Registration is open now across all four distances.
